Introduction
Data is vital for every business. IDC forecasts that the datasphere will double in size by 2026. Data will be ubiquitous and will keep growing exponentially in the future. Data generates insights that help run businesses, provides a competitive edge in the market, and enables employees to work together and stay efficient.
Today, data is used beyond the normal boundaries of busin

ess. Data is stored on-site, in multiple clouds, on devices, and more. It is being accessed from within and outside the corporate networks.
With the fast adoption and deployment of generative AI apps, more data will be produced at a faster rate. The risks involved in using and launching generative AI apps are not yet fully known and because of this they are increasing the demand for securing and governing the data input and output.
With this increase in data, data security incidents are common and rising, costing organizations millions of dollars every year to resolve.
Our customers need to secure and manage their data, but they often find it a complex and multi-faceted challenge.
Securing data is becoming harder as the data and its sources multiply - different kinds of data need different levels of protection. Applying general policies without knowing what data you have is not an efficient approach. It is estimated that about 30% of decision makers are unaware of the location or natur

e of their sensitive business-critical data, lacking full visibility in their digital estate.
Data does not move itself; people move data – it is important that organizations understand how data is being used and shared in their organization. Every organization has different kinds of data, different kinds of users, and they have different goals they want to achieve – there is no one size fits all strategy.
Organizations need to first understand the data security risks they face – this starts with getting visibility into what data they have, where it is stored and how their users are interacting with that data. Without this visibility, it is not possible to effectively protect the data.
This document contains delivery guidance for the Data Security Envisioning Workshop. The workshop will help customers understand data security risks related to their organizational data and offers a structured approach to mapping these risks to Microsoft Purview solutions that can help reduce the identif

ied risks while managing and protecting their data.

About the Data Security Envisioning Workshop
The Data Security Envisioning Workshop is a workshop delivered by Microsoft partners, Microsoft field, or Microsoft Global Partner Solutions (GPS) and its goal is to help land the value proposition of Microsoft Purview with customers’ business decision makers.
The workshop is built around a modular concept and provides delivery teams the option to add optional modules based on customer requirements and needs. The illustration below provides a high-level overview of both the mandatory and optional modules.
The activities will help customers assess their data security, privacy,

and regulatory requirements; address their most pressing data security goals and challenges; and provide an immersive experience that brings to life Microsoft’s vision and capabilities with respect to data security, privacy and regulatory compliance.
The objective for the Data Security Envisioning Workshop is to help customers understand how Microsoft 365 services and products can mitigate and protect against data security risks.
The Data Security Envisioning Workshop is powered by the Data Security Check. The Data Security Check is a structured activity that leverages a subset of Microsoft Purview products, services, and features to gain visibility into existing, and sometimes hidden, data security risks that may exist in the data that resides in the customer’s Microsoft 365 production environment. In addition to identifying data risks, the Data Security Check will also evaluate user behavior for risky activities that might impose risk to the organization. The outcome and findings of

the Data Security Check serve as input to the overall workshop and will be used to create awareness and identify potential areas for mitigation.
Qualification criteria for engagement funding
Partners delivering the Data Security Envisioning Workshop that want to qualify for the associated funding need to meet the overall qualification criteria as outlined on the customer nomination website. These partners must successfully deliver the following:
All Data Security Check mandatory modules.
At least one of the Data Security Check optional modules:
Compliance Manager
On-premises data scanner
Windows Endpoints
Communication Compliance
Data Security for AI
The Microsoft Purview portfolio overview
The Recommendations and next steps session.
Additionally, the partner can opt in to delivering one or more of the other Data Security Check optional modules.
Important
The delivery partner is free to decide on the modules delivered to the customer. However, failing to deliver any of the mandatory m

odules and at least one optional module will disqualify the delivery partner for the funding associated with the Data Security Envisioning Workshop.
At the conclusion of the Data Security Envisioning Workshop, both the customer and the delivery partner are required to complete and submit an online survey. Microsoft will review the submitted surveys for completeness and validate their content. The partner will only be eligible for funding associated with the workshop if both surveys are fully completed and accurate.
What is the Data Security Check?
The Data Security Check is an integral part of the Data Security Envisioning Workshop. The Data Security Check leverages Microsoft Purview tools and services in an automated process to:
Discover data that is stored in the Microsoft 365 Cloud and analyze it for the presence of artifacts that may impose data security risks to the organization.
Analyze user behavior for events that impose a risk to the customers organization. These vulnerabiliti

es include, but are not limited to, the loss of intellectual property, workplace harassment, oversharing of (sensitive) data, and the use of generative AI applications.
The Data Security Check is structured around typical Microsoft 365 services and their associated data repositories that organizations use. At its core, the Data Security Check analyzes user behavior and scans data repositories related to email, collaboration, and document storage. Optional modules can be added to extend the Data Security Check to include on-premises data repositories, Windows 10/11 endpoints, generative AI usage and more. All activities share a common set of activities for setup and configuration, write-up, and decommissioning as depicted in the illustration below.
The first activity for the Data Security Check is to enable and configure the tools and services needed for the Automated Discovery of data security risks. The Automated Discovery process will analyze user behavior for risky activity and scan

the data stored in the Microsoft Cloud for artifacts that might impose data security risks to the organization. The automated discovery process will run for approximately two to three weeks and will be followed by an analysis of the findings and identified risks. The last step of the engagement will be to present and deliver a set of recommendations that can help mitigate and eliminate the identified risks in the future.
The Automated Discovery process will:
Scan the existing data for the following artifacts:
Data that contains one or more sensitive information types
Documents, emails, real-time communication, and other types of data often contain critical information about employees, customers, projects, clients, or other types of business-sensitive content. Most organizations are, or will soon be, subject to one or more privacy or industry regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, SOX, HIPAA, or others. The unintended exposure, breach, or leakage of data containing any kind of sensitive infor

mation may potentially bring high financial, reputational, or other risks to the business and should be avoided at all times.
The Automated Discovery process will create an inventory of documents, files, and other types of data containing a variety of sensitive data including Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as credit card numbers, social security numbers, or personal health information (PHI). Additionally, by leveraging custom search terms, the Automated Discovery process will also search for business intellectual property such as business plans and product designs.
Stale data
Much of the data that is created by organizations becomes stale or unused immediately after creation and at that time is no longer of value. Most organizations have not implemented an automated retain and delete process to safeguard timely deletion of stale documents or data. This typically results in high volumes of stale and unused data that can impose risks and potential financial liability if c

onsumed by AI or exposed inappropriately. 
The Automated Discovery process will create an inventory of data that is older than 12 months and provides insight into the number of individual documents, their size, and location. This inventory can be used to better understand the risks of stale data and may even be used to optimize storage costs in the future by moving stale data to cheaper storage solutions.
Monitor user behavior for:
Suspicious and unusual activities
In addition to data discovery and analysis, the Data Security Check will also identify unusual activities involving organizational data such as a high volume of file uploads or downloads, unusual volume of external file sharing, IP Theft, sensitive data leaks or security violations.
What are the Data Security Check optional modules?
The Automated Discovery process focuses on identifying data security risks in data the customer has stored in the Microsoft 365 Cloud and analyzing user behavior for risky activity related to sen

sitive information. It can be extended by adding optional modules that will enhance the discovery process with capabilities to:
Assess the customer’s Microsoft 365 environment against the Data Protection Baseline and one or more customer specific assessments that can help the organization comply with national, regional, and industry-specific requirements governing the collection and use of data. (Compliance Manager module).
Scan on-premises data repositories such as file shares and SharePoint Server libraries. (On-premises data scanner module).
Detect malicious and inadvertent risk activities on local workstations. (Windows Endpoints module)
Discover privacy and regulatory risks by evaluating user communication inside the organization. (Communication Compliance module).
Analyze user access to Generative AI solutions like Microsoft 365 Copilot and third-party AI websites. Highlight issues with shadow AI use, sensitive information exposure, and potential data oversharing. (Data Security

for AI module)
The partner delivering the Data Security Check should engage in a dialog with the customer to discuss the optional modules and decide which are relevant to the them and should be included in the Data Security Check scope.
Important
To qualify for the funding associated to the delivery of the Data Security Envisioning Workshop, at least one optional module must be delivered.
The Microsoft Purview portfolio overview
The Microsoft Purview portfolio overview will be delivered as part of the Data Security Envisioning Workshop. During this session, the delivery partner will introduce the customer to the Microsoft Purview vision and outline Microsoft’s approach to providing integrated protection and risk mitigation.
By using the findings from the Data Security Check Automated Discovery, the Microsoft Purview portfolio overview presentation will be tailored to the customer’s situation and provide real life examples of services that can help mitigate data security risks.
The Reco

mmendations and next steps activity
Recommendations and next steps typically is the last activity for the Data Security Envisioning Workshop. During this session the findings and risks that were identified by the Data Security Check are mapped to products and services from the Microsoft Purview portfolio and actionable next steps are defined and presented.
Data confidentiality and information privacy
To safeguard user and data privacy and prevent access to sensitive or personal search results by unauthorized customer or partner staff, inventory data and content identified by the Automated Discovery process is only accessible to authenticated and authorized users who have been assigned the appropriate access privileges. Where applicable, pseudonymization will be used to further protect user privacy. Additionally, all activities involving data or content will be logged and are auditable.

Data Security Envisioning Workshop-Overview
The Data Security Envisioning Workshop, powered by the Data Security Check, is an engagement delivered by Microsoft field, Microsoft Global Pa

The engagement is structured around three core activities and preceded by a Pre-engagement meeting to discuss the upcoming activities, resource requirements, and delivery schedule.
On-site vs. remote delivery
The Data Security Envisioning Workshop can be delivered remotely through online meetings or on-site at the customer’s premises. On-site delivery is the preferred delivery method because of the highly interactive nature of the engagement and configuration activities.

Data Security Check
Guidance
The Data Security Check is the core activity of the Data Security Envisioning Workshop. It leverages Microsoft 365 Cloud technology to identify risks in the organizational data. The findings and risks identified by the Data Security Check will be presented and discussed during the workshop and will be used as a conversation starter for follow-up discussions on risk mitigation and improving the customer’s compliance posture
The Data Security Check acti

vities are designed to be delivered over a three-week period and are organized around the different data locations that typically exist within the customer’s cloud based productivity environment (e.g. Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, etc.). The illustration below provides a high-level overview of all activities that are required to set up, configure, and run the Data Security Check, and the following paragraphs will describe the activities in greater detail.
The Data Security Check includes three types of activities:
Core activities. Core activities such as configuring Sensitive Info Types and exporting log files and reports are required for both the mandatory and the optional modules.
Mandatory activities. A delivery of the Data Security Envisioning Workshop should always include all mandatory activities. Completing the mandatory activities is the primary eligibility requirement for engagement funding.
Optional activities. Optional activities are part of the modules that can

be added to the engagement scope based on specific customer ask or opportunity.
Objectives
The objectives for the Data Security Check are:
Discover data security risks.
Gain visibility into existing, and at sometimes hidden, data security risks that might exist in the customer’s organizational data.
Understand how to mitigate identified risks.
Help customers to better understand, prioritize, and mitigate the identified risks across the Microsoft Cloud and optionally on-premises data repositories.
Provide recommendations and define next steps.
Scoping
In scope
The default Data Security Check scope includes:
Gain visibility into hidden data security risks in the Microsoft 365 Cloud environment in use by the customer.
Enable the Automated Discovery service to search for:
Data that contains one or more sensitive information types
Stale data
Suspicious and unusual activities
Help the customer understand how Microsoft Purview products and services can help mitigate and protect against the d

ata security risks that were identified over the course of the engagement.
Enable Microsoft 365 services used by the Data Security Check Automated Discovery process:
Microsoft Purview eDiscovery
Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
Microsoft Purview Information Protection
Microsoft Purview Audit
In addition to the default scope, additional Microsoft Purview products and services can be enabled to extend the engagement to include other data repositories and user activities:
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention for Endpoints
Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner
Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance
Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management for AI (DSPM for AI)
Out of scope
The standard scope of the engagement excludes:
Discovery activities for other cloud services. The Data Security Check does not include discovery activities for third-party cloud services such as, but not limited

to, AWS, Box, and Google Drive.
Proof of concept or lab deployment. The standard scope of the Data Security Check does not include deployment of the solution in a development or proof of concept environment.
Creation of a data labelling taxonomy. The standard scope of the Data Security Check does not include defining and designing a data labeling taxonomy.
Creation of data retention policies or schedules. The standard scope of the Data Security Check does not include marking any data discovered during the Automated Discovery for retention or deletion.
Labeling discovered documents or data. The standard scope of the Data Security Check does not include applying labels to data or documents identified during the Automated Discovery.
Client discovery activities. The Data Security Check standard scope does not include discovery activities that involve client devices such as, but not limited to, workstations, laptops, mobile devices (this can however be added as an optional module).

Sensitive Info Types
Sensitive Info Types are the artifacts the Data Security Check Automated Discovery

process will look for in various Microsoft 365 storage locations such as Exchange Online, OneDrive for Business, and SharePoint Online or when evaluating user behavior, user communication or interaction with generative AI tools (optional). Microsoft 365 comes with over 315 pre-defined Out-of-box Sensitive Info Types that are ready to use by the Automated Discovery process described in this guide. In addition, this guide will describe how to create Custom Sensitive Info Types that meet the customer’s specific needs.
The discovery capabilities of the automated process depend on the storage location, the type of activity and the type of data.
Storage locations
The Automated Discovery works across the following storage locations:
Exchange Online: Used for mailboxes, public folders, Teams conversations, Viva Engage (Yammer) user messages, and Microsoft 365 group mailboxes.
SharePoint Online: Used for SharePoint Online sites, OneDrive for Business accounts, Teams sites, Viva Engage (Yammer)

networks, and Microsoft 365 Group sites.
Teams: Used for chat and channel messages, including private channels.
This delivery guide will provide guidance on how to configure the Automated Discovery for both out-of-the-box and custom Sensitive Info Types. The examples provided should be customized to align with your customer’s expectations and requirements. If needed, additional or more complex search queries can be defined and added.

Impact on user experience
The Data Security Check Automated Discovery process will be fully transparent to both the end user and administrator; it will not modify, move, or delete any data:
eDiscovery will only search for and report on stale data across the Microsoft Cloud in use by

the organization; it will not delete, archive, or apply other types of retention policies to the data.
Data Loss Prevention will only report on data containing the sensitive items configured; it will not send notifications to the end user, prevent sharing, implement encryption, or apply other changes to the data.
Insider Risk Management will only report on insider risks; it will not send notifications to the end user, prevent sharing, implement encryption, or apply other changes to the data.
Compliance Manager will only advise and recommend on improvement actions, it will not implement any changes to the customer production environment.
Data Loss Prevention for Endpoints will only scan for risky behavior on client workstations; it will not block any actions or change the end user experience in any way. Data Loss Prevention for Endpoints will leverage standard Windows 10/11 services and does not require the installation of agents on the user’s workstation.
Purview Information Protection

scanner will only scan for privacy and regulatory risks in on-premises data repositories; the scanner will not apply, modify, or remove labels.
Communication Compliance will monitor communications for sharing of information that can impose risk or vulnerability to the organization; it will not block any actions or change the end user experience in any way.
DSPM for AI will only monitor interactions with generative AI applications and report on activities that can impose risk to the organization; it will not block or prevent any interaction with such tools or applications.
Important
Carefully follow the provided guidance and do not configure additional options or services because they might have an impact on the user experience.

Step 4 - Analyze the findings
Guidance
The Automated Discovery process will log findings to several reports and log files. To prepare for analysis, the reports and logs must be downloaded and made available. The following paragraphs provide step-by-step instructions on how to export and download the files needed and how to create screenshots, pivot tables, and other illustrations that can be used to visualize the findings during the close-out presentation.
Important
The time needed for exporting reports and log files depends on the number of issues identified by the Automated Discovery process. It is recommended to perform the in

structions in this section at least one day prior to analysis activities.
Once the reports and log files are collected and stored in the newly created local folders, the analysis of the findings can begin. It is recommended to start the analysis process by looking at the various dashboards available from the Microsoft Purview portal. These dashboards will provide high-level insights into the findings and allow you to quickly identify trends and high-impact risks.
What to look for in reports generated by the Automated Discovery process
The Data Security Check focuses on identifying data security risks related to organizational data and risky user activities. We expect Automated Discovery to identify risks related to:
Personally Identifiable Information (PII), such as passport numbers, social security numbers, social insurance numbers, health service numbers, or taxpayer numbers.
Financial data, such as bank accounts numbers or credit cards.
Custom specific sensitive data, defined specif

ically for the customer, such as employee records, salary information, record updates, confidential projects or documents, product specifications, or company IP.
User behaviors, such as the improper handling of sensitive information, accidental (or deliberate) leakage or destruction of data, or inappropriate, harmful, or unauthorized communications.
Interaction with generative AI applications, such as access to Microsoft 365 Copilot and/or third-party generative AI websites and the use of unmanaged or unsanctioned third-party generative AI websites.
The Automated Discovery looks sensitive data types that are:
Stored in:
Exchange Online
SharePoint Online
OneDrive for Business
Sent over email connections to other recipients.
Stored in locations that are shared with external organizations/people.
Processed on Windows Endpoints.
Sent as Microsoft Teams chat and channel messages, including private channel messages.
Shared with generative AI applications.

The Automated Discovery finding

s will contain personal identifiable and sensitive corporate information. Organizations may request to first do an internal analysis before handing the information over for further investigation.
